headline: Angers have conceded 10 in two — and Lorient arrive after beating Monaco
summary: Angers have conceded 10 goals in their last two Ligue 1 matches — 1-5 at Brest, then 2-5 at home to Marseille on Sunday. Next they host Lorient, who beat league leaders Monaco 1-0 last week. Angers are still without midfielder Haris Belkebla, who missed the Marseille defeat. The market has followed those results: Lorient's win chance rose from 33.9% to 39.3%. Even so, the gap stays small — on the fair handicap line Lorient are a quarter of a goal better, 0.15 — and few goals are expected, with under 2.5 at 52.8%.
read: Angers have shipped ten goals in two matches — 1-5 at Brest and 2-5 at home to Marseille — and now host a Lorient team that beat leaders Monaco 1-0 last week, led by Angers' former coach Alexandre Dujeux. The market has followed the results: Lorient are now the favourites, rated about 0.15 goals the better side, with under 2.5 goals the lean at 52.8%.

facts.fact: Angers have conceded ten goals in their last two Ligue 1 matches — 1-5 at Brest, then 2-5 at home to Marseille on Sunday.
facts.meaning: They go into a home game as the leakiest side in the division on current form, with the midfield and back line under pressure.

facts.fact: Lorient beat league leaders Monaco 1-0 on matchday 7 — their third win in five league games.
facts.meaning: They arrive with the far better recent record and the confidence of having just beaten the best team in the table.

facts.fact: Lorient's win chance has risen from 33.9% to 39.3% since Sunday, while Angers' has slipped the other way.
facts.meaning: A match that was near even four days ago now has a clear away favourite.

facts.fact: The handicap fair line sits at Angers +0.15 — the market now rates Lorient a fraction of a goal the better side, after Angers were rated marginally ahead before the weekend.
Angers sit 15th of 18 in Ligue 1 after seven matches.
facts.meaning: A home defeat here keeps them in the bottom third and turns a bad week into a bad start.

facts.fact: Under 2.5 goals is the market lean at 52.8%.
facts.meaning: The market expects a tight, low-scoring game even though Angers have just shipped ten goals in two matches.

facts.fact: Lorient average 1.16 xG per game across their last five matches — modest chance creation for a side that has won three of them.
facts.meaning: Their wins are built on defending and fine margins, so if they win here it is more likely to be by one goal than by a scoreline.

facts.fact: Haris Belkebla, who missed the Marseille defeat through injury, was still absent from Angers training four days before kick-off.
facts.meaning: Angers are likely without another option in the middle as they try to protect a defence that has conceded ten in two.

sources.fact: Angers have conceded ten goals in their last two matches, including a 2-5 home defeat to Marseille.
Angers lost 2-5 at home to Marseille in Ligue 1 on matchday 7.
Haris Belkebla, who missed the Marseille match through injury, is still absent from Angers training four days before facing Lorient.
Ousmane Camara, who was absent against Marseille, has returned to training with the Angers squad.
Emmanuel Biumla is training away from the Angers first-team group and is doubtful to face Lorient.
Angers sit on 7 points after seven matches and view the visit of Lorient as an immediate chance to respond after the Marseille defeat.
Lorient beat Monaco 1-0 on matchday 7, handing the leaders their first defeat of the season.
Alexandre Dujeux, Lorient's current coach, is Angers' former coach and will face his old club.
